//: Latin. Every id of i18n/eng.json is defined here too, in the same tables; its notes apply here as well. No watch can be set to Latin (System.Language has no Latin), so only the language picker's "Latina" reads these texts: Automatic never does. The names of the prayers, the mystery sets and the mysteries are taken from the Holy See's Latin texts, without the stress accents they print over some words and with ae for their æ, as the Vulgate text here writes it; the UI phrases are plain ecclesiastical Latin. Every source URL is in odd/tasks/latin-language.md.

glance.//: The set names in the plural, as Rosarium Virginis Mariae and the Compendium of the Catechism name the sets (mysteria gaudiosa, dolorosa, gloriosa, luminosa), the noun left out as in the other languages. PrayerSalve is the Compendium's title of the prayer, written without its comma ("Salve, Regina") as the prayer's title usually is.

ui.// PrayerCreed: The prayers as the Compendium of the Catechism's appendix of Latin prayers titles them: "Pater Noster", "Ave Maria", "Gloria Patri". The Compendium writes "Ave, Maria"; the label leaves the comma out, as the prayer's title usually does. The Creed, which it titles "Symbolum Apostolicum", is named by its first word, "Credo", as in Spanish.
ui.// PrayerFatima: The Fatima Prayer has no official Latin text: its first words, "Domine Iesu", are those of the Latin EWTN publishes ("Oratio Fatimae").
ui.// MysteryTitle: The ordinal, then the noun and the set's adjective, both in the singular (Primum mysterium gaudiosum). Beside the lens each word takes a line of its own, and the first line of the reading view's and the menu's title holds at most 72px: so the second is "Alterum", Latin's other ordinal for second, since "Secundum" (76px) runs into the bezel there.
ui.// LanguageAutomatic: Feminine, as it stands for a lingua, like "Latina" (the picker's name of this language, in source/LanguageView.mc).

mysteries.//: The joyful, sorrowful and glorious mysteries as the Compendium of the Catechism's appendix names them under "Rosarium". "Agonia in Horto" corrects its misprint "Agonia in Hortu" (hortus, ablative horto). The luminous mysteries as Rosarium Virginis Mariae (21) lists them, in the nominative: "Regni Dei proclamatio" leaves out "coniuncta cum invitamento ad conversionem", as the English name leaves out the call to conversion, so that it fits 2 lines.

// quotes: Source: the Vulgata Clementina (public domain), in the text of the Clementine Text Project as Bible Gateway publishes it (version VULGATE, https://www.biblegateway.com/versions/Biblia-Sacra-Vulgata-VULGATE/); one URL per quote in odd/tasks/latin-language.md. Each quote is copied verbatim from the verse text there, and drbo.org's Latin Vulgate has the same words. Each excerpt is the English quote's, clause for clause. "…" marks an excerpt that starts or ends inside a sentence, so the Latin has one where its sentence goes on past the English excerpt's full stop (Lc 1, 48; Io 19, 17; Lc 24, 6). Lc 22, 19 stops before "hoc facite in meam commemorationem": the reading window, 132px wide, cannot show "commemorationem." (144px), and a word is never split. The references use the Vulgate's verse numbering, as the Douay-Rheims does (the voice from the cloud is Mark 9:6), and the abbreviations of the Holy See's Latin documents.
